blocking.what: Each `## Restrictions` block carries a five-row table (`[R1]`–`[R5]`) although the operator's restriction file does not exist and lists none.
blocking.why: The guidelines require that, with no restriction file or a file that lists none, the block carries the sentence `No specific restrictions apply to the **MaxPool** operator.` and no table; the rows are copied from the file, not composed by the writer.
blocking.fix: Delete the table from all four `## Restrictions` blocks and add the sentence `No specific restrictions apply to the **MaxPool** operator.` after the general-restrictions link in each.

blocking.what: The general-restrictions link is written `[General restrictions](./../common/general_restrictions.md) are applicable.`
blocking.why: The guidelines fix the link target as `./global_restrictions.md`; the profile's global file is `global_restrictions.md`, and the document points at a path that does not exist.
blocking.fix: Replace the link with `[General restrictions](./global_restrictions.md) are applicable.` in every family section.

blocking.what: The formula `Y[...] = max_{k_0,...,k_{m-1}} X_p[...]` takes the maximum over the window indices $k_t \in [0, dK_t-1]$ of the padded tensor $X_p$, and the padded elements are excluded only by the prose that follows.
blocking.why: The formula as written is not a total function of the window: it applies `max` to padded positions that are not elements of $X$, so a reader must choose what value a padded element contributes. The case is decided by the prose, but the formula and the prose must be one statement; as it stands the formula alone is undefined on the padded region.
blocking.fix: Restrict the index set in the formula itself, e.g. take the maximum over the $k_t$ such that $j_t \cdot s_t + k_t - p_{t,\text{begin}}$ lies in $[0, dX_{t+2}-1]$ for every $t$, and keep the prose sentence as the explanation of that restriction.

blocking.what: The `[R4]` row reads "Attribute `dilations` is restricted to $1$ along each spatial axis", but the operator's restriction file gives `[R4]` as "The padding of a spatial axis is at most the size of the kernel along that axis, i.e. $p^b_k \le k_k$ and $p^e_k \le k_k$ for every spatial axis $k$".
blocking.why: The rows of `ops/maxpool_restrictions.md` are copied into every family section verbatim and in the file's order; a reworded row is a finding (checklist, per restrictions).
blocking.fix: Replace the `[R4]` row in all four `## Restrictions` tables with the file's row verbatim: `| `[R4]` | The padding of a spatial axis is at most the size of the kernel along that axis, i.e. $p^b_k \le k_k$ and $p^e_k \le k_k$ for every spatial axis $k$ | Transient |`.

blocking.section: ## Function (real, float, int, uint) and ## Inputs / ## Outputs
blocking.what: The restriction `[R4]` (padding at most the kernel size) is nowhere reflected in the semantics: the Function section, the `pads` attribute and the `E_MAXPOOL_*_CONSTR_X_0020` window-coverage constraint all allow $p_{t,\text{begin}} + p_{t,\text{end}} \ge dK_t$ with no upper bound on either padding.
blocking.why: The consequence of a restriction that bears on the operator is stated where the semantics are stated; a section that contradicts a restriction is a finding (checklist, per restrictions).
blocking.fix: State the bound in the `pads` attribute description and in the window-coverage constraint (e.g. add `$p_{t,\text{begin}} \le dK_t$ and $p_{t,\text{end}} \le dK_t$` to the statement of `E_MAXPOOL_<FAM>_CONSTR_X_0020`), so that the Function section's padding paragraph no longer admits paddings the restriction forbids.

blocking.what: The float section's case analysis of the maximum does not decide the case of a window that covers both $+\text{inf}$ and $-\text{inf}$: it says $+\text{inf}$ is greater than every finite value and than $-\text{inf}$, and that a window whose elements are all $-\text{inf}$ gives $-\text{inf}$, but the mixed case is left to the reader.
blocking.why: Every case that applies to the operator is decided by the specification or declared open; the special values of the floating-point types as operands and as results are among the cases that shall be stated (Function, part 2).
blocking.fix: Add one sentence to the float case analysis: a window that covers $+\text{inf}$ gives $+\text{inf}$, whatever the other elements of the window are.
